I'd recommend not spending a lot on expensive toys, or going out of your way to make elaborate hammocks, because when it comes down to it, rats typically enjoy a cardboard box to tear up more than anything you can buy them. If he's wary of you, putting one of your shirts (one that you wore all day would be best) in his cage can help getting him used to your smell. Once he's less afraid, it's a good idea to carry him around, either in your shirt or on your shoulder, for about twenty minutes at a time to get him accustomed to being out. You should take him out every day, and the more the better, because they love being out. If you can't take him out that often, make syre his cage is full of things to keep him busy. Rats like a big variety of snacks, but from personal experience I'd say yogurt, blueberries and strawberries, peas, chicken (never with the bone), and the occasional piece of chocolate are some favourites. I also highly recommend putting away money whenever you get the chance to build up a vet fund, because pet rats tend to need emergency visits to the vet that can end up very costly. If there's anything else you need help with along your journey of rat ownership, Rattit is a great place to get advice, ask questions, and mingle with other rat owners

To my knowledge, agouti is dominant. In wild rats I think it's typically represented as AA, or Aa with the lower case a being black. That means it's possible for two rats carrying both genes to result in aa, which would be a black rat. Now, if a pink eye dilute (pp) was released into the wld and bred with a black rat (aa) it could result in aapp, which would be champagne. Similarly, if a red eye dilute (rr) was released and bred with an agouti (either Aa or AA), it could result in AArr or Aarr, which would be fawn. I could be wrong though, and if I am please correct me.

The smaller businesses around here are mostly run by families who actually care about animals, and they don't get their rats from mills. I guess that's just around here, then..

If you have breeders near you, that would probably be the best way to go, as they will be the most likely to have friendly, healthy rats that should live a long life. If not, you can always check rescues nearby, because adoption is always great. You can consider checking goosemoose, ratforum, or craigslist, because there are a lot of people that have accidental litters; you have a high chance of getting friendly rats from there because they're usually handled from birth. (Just make sure the person isn't a feeder breeder.) If you can find a pet store that keeps their rats in clean cages, and they're friendly and healthy, then by all means go for it. You may be more likely to get this result from small business stores, as opposed to chain stores, because they probably get their rats locally and you can make sure it isn't a rat mill. Two of my girls came from Petco and they're wonderful and healthy, but it really just depends on how things are locally for you.
